trap_families.required_sqlserver_check: Declare SQL Server collation and PG normalization/collation; include uniqueness.
Compare SQL Server padding rules separately for equality, LIKE and binary collations.
LEN excludes trailing U+0020; preserve leading/internal spaces and NULL.
Check SQL Server integer division and precedence; do not promote integers implicitly.
First-argument type/length drives SQL Server ISNULL truncation; ASE is not authority.
SQL Server empty numeric/date conversion differs from both ASE storage and PG casts.
SQL Server datetime grid, range and displayed milliseconds require separate observations.
SQL Server counts unit boundaries rather than whole elapsed units.
Bind DATEFIRST, DATEFORMAT and conversion styles; don't reuse ASE defaults.
Check signed ties, negative scales and money intermediate precision on SQL Server.
SQL Server caught statement failure need not roll back prior work; PG EXCEPTION subtransaction does.
Bind XACT_ABORT and entry/exit @@TRANCOUNT; no wrapper rollback.
Severity <=10 is informational; approved message/error mapping required.
SCOPE_IDENTITY differs from @@IDENTITY with triggers; sequences also advance on rollback.
@@ROWCOUNT changes after intervening statements; capture DONE_IN_PROC separately.
Explicit map between ordered TDS result sets and PG refcursors/OUT sets.
Capture OUTPUT values and default return 0 independently of result sets.
Several matching update sources leave the selected row unspecified; policy/repeated-run required.
Qualify matched/unmatched effects and duplicate-source errors on exact engine versions.
Local procedure temp scope and table variables differ from persistent PG session temp tables.
Inventory-only ASE unsupported status does not establish SQL Server support; preserve parameter binding.
@@FETCH_STATUS is connection-scoped and can be changed by nested cursors.
Multirow inserted/deleted facts must match statement semantics, not per-row assumptions.
SQL Server bit/uniqueidentifier are not ASE timestamp rowversions; explicit canonical types.
TOP without ORDER BY always requires a policy; a coincidental matching row is not equivalence.
